newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Wednesday on profit-taking, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at 3,384 yuan ($408) per tonne, losing 14 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,475 and hit a low of 3,345.
The May contract fell six yuan to 3,427, September fell 23 to 3,385, November fell two to 3,410, the January 1998 contract fell 29 to 3,370, March fell 20 to 3,375.
Combined volume fell to 9,300 tonnes from 15,500 the previous session.
Soybeans opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices steadily down for most of the session, traders said.
"Profit-taking is responsible for today's falls, but volume was thin, indicating further heavy losses are unlikely," one trader said.
"Soybeans are likely to continue consolidating over the next few days due to a lack of market-moving news," he said.
Traders said they were suggesting to retail investors that they remain on the sidelines in the short term.
